memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: Then the Lord said to Joshua: "Tell the Israelites to designate the cities of refuge, as I instructed you through Moses, so that anyone who kills a person accidentally and unintentionally may flee there and find protection from the avenger of blood." - Josh 20:1-3 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
God gives Joshua a tender and remarkable command: set apart cities of refuge. In those days, if someone was killed, the nearest relative — the "avenger of blood" — had the right and duty to pursue the one responsible. But what about a person who killed someone accidentally, with no hatred or intent? Without protection, they could be struck down for a tragic mistake. So God, in His mercy, provided cities where such a person could flee and be safe.

This reveals so much about the heart of God. He is perfectly just — He takes the loss of human life seriously, for every person bears His image. But He is also merciful, distinguishing between deliberate murder and tragic accident. He made careful provision to protect the one who had caused harm without meaning to. Justice and mercy meet in this arrangement, neither cancelling the other.

We serve a God who is both just and merciful still. He does not overlook wrong, yet He makes a way of refuge for those who need it. And this points forward wonderfully to Christ. Just as the accidental manslayer could flee to a city of refuge and find safety, so we, guilty and pursued by the weight of our sin, can flee to Jesus and find refuge in Him. The writer of Hebrews speaks of those who "have fled to take hold of the hope set before us" (Heb 6:18). Christ is our refuge, where mercy shelters us from the judgment we could not survive alone.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
- Do you see both the justice and the mercy of God in the cities of refuge?
- Where do you need to flee to Christ as your refuge from sin's weight?
- How does knowing God provides refuge change how you approach Him?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, thank You that You are both perfectly just and wonderfully merciful. Like the one fleeing to the city of refuge, I run to Christ, my refuge and safety. Hold me there. Amen.
